extracted.intended_audience: readers of travel and natural-history narrative; aspiring field naturalists and collectors
extracted.subtask_description: Producing first-person travel or natural-history chapters that combine field observations, ethnographic detail, and practical collecting logistics. Emphasizes accurate description, anecdotal scenes, and advice for specimen-gathering in remote regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize truthful representation; avoid flattering embellishment
rubrics_metrics.description: “And here I might (if I followed the example of most travellers) launch out into a glowing description of the charms of these damsels... But, alas! regard for truth will not permit me to expatiate too admiringly on such topics, determined as I am to give as far as I can a true picture of the people and places I visit.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not romanticize or over-embellish subjects for effect; aim for an honest, measured portrayal even where flowery descriptions would be conventional. Example/anti-pattern: avoid stock phrases like “sparkling eyes” and “tiny feet” when they would misrepresent the scene. Truthfulness to observed reality is a guiding principle for credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise, concrete observational detail (including scientific names and behaviors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text supplies many specific details and taxa (e.g., “the cream-coloured pigeon, Carpophaga luctuosa,” “the blue-headed roller, Coracias temmincki,” variety of Ornithoptera, and notes on insect and bird habits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor descriptions with concrete particulars—species names, distinctive behaviours, colours, textures, and local habitat—so the account reads as authoritative and informative rather than vague. Where relevant, include technical names and observable actions to support claims and interest specialist readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include practical fieldcraft and procedural logistics for collecting
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative includes procedural details: secure letters of introduction and permission from local rulers; hire local assistants (boys who can skin birds, carry nets); plan seasonally (avoid wet season for drying collections); and protect specimens practically (suspend insect-box over water/oil to stop ants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing natural-history travel pieces, incorporate concrete logistical advice so the account serves both as narrative and field guide: how to obtain permissions, manage local help, pack and protect specimens, and time collecting around seasons. These practical notes increase usefulness and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show local customs and social relations through scenes and anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: The author conveys social detail by scene: audience with the Rajah (letter sewn in yellow silk), the village ‘bitchara’ where tobacco and five rupees are offered, children bringing shells for payment, and villagers’ reactions to the European as an ‘ogre’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer episodic scenes, small interactions, and concrete gestures to summarize customs and social structures—use dialogues, exchanges, and sensory moments to reveal culture rather than abstract exposition. Anecdotes that illustrate reciprocity, ritual, or daily practices make social description vivid and believable.
